newClaim.name: Sound and noise in context
newClaim.subject: Science
newClaim.sourceInterpretation: Bounded everyday contextual unwanted/interfering-sound interpretation; not claimed to be an explicit NCERT publisher definition. Actual surrounding source and complete pinned-source text contain no contrary ordered/irregular-vibration definition.

whyReuseFails.mt__00ZSLnB7p: Amplitude/loudness and source-vibration relation do not classify contextual unwantedness.
whyReuseFails.mt_KTSoXcO7OL: Pitch and object-vibration patterns do not supply the distinction.
whyReuseFails.mt_VBl1T1sFCM: Sound-making and sound-to-matter vibration do not supply listener/activity context.
whyReuseFails.mt_YPSx5pbpVl: Full light/sound word inventory omits the noise concept.
whyReuseFails.mt_S0hzjAeLSK: A reasoned opinion can be expressed without knowing that noise is sound or that the same sound may be noise in a changed context.
whyReuseFails.mt_wzUzVEBqJb: Different feelings are recognised without the sound/noise category or its task-interference application.

newClaim.independentCounterexample: A learner can explain vibrations and loudness/pitch, justify a preference for a song and accept another listener’s dislike, yet treat noise as not-sound or classify every instrument as never-noise. Those whole existing operations do not entail the source distinction.
newClaim.wholeClaimPositive: Use only gentle recordings or fictional sound-scene descriptions. A short bell is requested as an agreed activity signal; the identical bell interrupts a recorded character’s quiet conversation after the signal is no longer needed. The learner classifies and explains the difference in supplied purpose, retaining noise-as-sound.
nearMisses: Calls noise a different non-sound substance.
Says every loud sound is noise, including the explicitly requested signal, without considering the purpose.
Says an instrument can never be noise, or a machine always is, despite supplied listener/activity information.
Only reports an own preference without explaining the contextual distinction.
newClaim.transfer: A character requests a gentle musical practice sound in a lesson; another fictional character later requests quiet for listening to a story. Explain the status of the same recording without judging either person’s taste as wrong.
newClaim.guide: Complete original, untested, low-confidence guide in data/teaching-research.json.
